set.tovw: Robber's buried-loot story was a ruse; money recovered from his cap the same day
set.st: Aug 16 1924: Clayton Raub, 28, of Elkhart robbed the Trufant State Bank of $500+ and was caught. He said he had buried the money and his gun between two houses in Pierson, 7 mi W of Trufant, and an early AP story reported a failed search. The Detroit Free Press (18 Aug 1924) gives the outcome: when the sheriff took him to the spot he knocked off his cap and the money fell out. 'It never left Raub's cap'; the gun likewise. Nothing was ever buried. Pin marks the story only. Independent listing: Pierson (MI gazetteer 1881: place, 44 listings).
set.t: Look-only story marker: the loot was recovered the same day and nothing was buried. Access: town lots: permission.

src: Detroit Free Press, 18 Aug 1924, p. 9 (newspapers.com 1049344277): money fell from Raub's cap; nothing buried
